Bahola people recall brutal killing of 32 by Pak army
2014-12-14T00:00:00+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Dinajpur
https://www.thedailystar.net/bahola-people-recall-brutal-killing-of-32-by-pak-army-55189

'Bahola tragedy day' was observed in Biral upazila of the district yesterday.

During the Liberation War in 1971, Pakistan occupation army and their collaborators massacred at least 32 people at Bahola village.

Remembering the victims a memorial was built in 2012 at the spot, but the graveyard still remains in utter neglect.

During a visit to the spot, this correspondent found that the mass graveyard getting damaged while cattle, goats and dogs moving freely in the area. The surrounded walls of the graveyard also mostly collapsed.

Like every year, people of Biral upazila observe the day by holding different programmes including discussion, offering prayers at mosques and temples.

According to the eyewitnesses and family members, at least 32 people were brutally killed by Pakistani troops at Bahola with the help of their Bangladeshi collaborators on the day.

Later, the bodies were dumped in a ditch at the village, they said.

Local elderly people said, the Pakistani troops started to retreat from Bochaganj upazila toward Biral and Dinajpur as the upazila was freed on December 6 after a fierce fighting with Indian troops and freedom fighters.

On December 12 night, the Pakistani troops entered Bahola and asked the villagers to help nab the freedom fighters of the area as there were two freedom fighter camps at Bahola and Palashbari villages, said villager Rafiqul Islam.

As the villagers declined to provide any information regarding the freedom fighters, the Pakistani troops and their collaborators on December 13 carried out the brutal killing.
